ἀγαπάω.text: ἀγαπάω, I love (never of love between the sexes, but nearly always of the love of (the) God or (the) Christ to us, and of our love to Him and to our fellow creatures, as inspired by His love for us).

ἀγάπη.text: ἀγάπη (a word exclusively Biblical, curtailed from ἀγάπησις [from ἀγαπάω]: in LXX generally of sexual love; first in higher sense not before about 100 B.C.), love [this was the sense of the word charity in the time of the A.V.], as that of (the) God or (the) Christ to us, and our love to Him and to our fellow creatures thus inspired: ἀγάπη τοῦ θεοῦ, τοῦ χριστοῦ are sometimes ambiguous, when it is doubtful whether (the) God's, (the) Christ's love for us, or our love for (the) God, (the) Christ, is intended; in most cases the former is probably the primary thought: ἀγάπαι plur. (Jude, verse 12) concr., of the love-feasts of the Christians, evening meals partaken of by Christians in the early Church, either accompanied or followed by the Eucharist. Such common meals were sacred, and intended to be expressive of the union of Christians in their Head.

ἀγαθός.text: ἀγαθός, (intrinsically) good, good (in nature), good (whether it be seen to be so or not), the widest and most colourless of all words with this meaning (opp. πονηρός, κακός): τὰ ἀγαθά (bona), the goods, Lk. xii 18.

ἀγαλλιάω.text: ἀγαλλιάω, I exult, I am full of joy.

ἅγιος.text: ἅγιος, set apart by (or for) the God, holy, sacred, e.g. ἁγία πόλις (of Jerusalem) Mt. iv 5; τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα, practically synonymous with τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ θεοῦ; ὁ ἅγιος τοῦ θεοῦ (Mk. i 24) of the Messiah; οἱ ἅγιοι, of the Christians as the new people of God, taking the place of the Hebrews: τὸ ἅγιον, τὰ ἅγια, the temple; τὰ ἅγια τῶν ἁγίων, the inmost part of the temple, the inner shrine.

ἄγγελος.text: ἄγγελος, a messenger, generally: a (supernatural) messenger from God, an angel, conveying news or behests from (the) God to men: almost an intermediary, Gal. iii 19.

ἀγαπητός.text: ἀγαπητός, loved, beloved, with two special applications, (a) ὁ ἀγαπητός, the Beloved, a title of the Messiah (Christ), as beloved beyond all others by the God who sent Him; (b) of Christians, as beloved by God, Christ, and one another.

ἁγιάζω.text: ἁγιάζω (apparently exclusively Biblical), I make ἅγιος, treat as ἅγιος (set apart, holy), sanctify, hallow (see ἅγιος).

ἁγιασμός.text: ἁγιασμός, the process of making or becoming ἅγιος (set apart, holy).

ἀγνοέω.text: ἀγνοέω, I do not know, I am ignorant of (a person, thing, or fact), sometimes with the idea of wilful ignorance.

ἁγνός.text: ἁγνός (originally, in a condition prepared for worship), pure (either ethically, or ritually, ceremonially); chaste.

ἁγνίζω.text: ἁγνίζω, I make pure, either (a) ceremonially (e.g. Ac. xxi 24), or (b) actually (e.g. 1 Pet. i 22).

ἄγω.text: ἄγω, (a) I lead, I lead away, I bring (a person, or animal); thus I bring before a court of justice; (b) especially in 1st pers. plur. subjunct. ἄγωμεν, intr. let us depart (e.g. Mk. i 38); (c) I hold, keep, celebrate: ἀγοραῖοι ἄγονται (Ac. xix 38), assizes are held.

ἀγρός.text: ἀγρός (a word rare in papyrus documents, and now obsolete), a field, especially as bearing a crop; the country, Mk. xv 21, xvi 12: plur. ἀγροί, lands, property in land, a country estate.

ἀγών.text: ἀγών, an (athletic) contest; hence, a struggle (in the soul).

ἀδελφός.text: ἀδελφός, (a) a brother (so probably even in Rom. xvi 23, 2 Cor. xii 18); (b) (a use characteristic of Jewish literature but not confined to it) a member of the same religious community, especially a fellow-Christian (particularly in the plural).

ἀδικέω.text: ἀδικέω, I act unjustly towards, I injure, I harm (animate or inanimate).

ἀδελφή.text: ἀδελφή, (a) a sister; (b) a woman (fellow-)member of a church, a Christian woman (Rom. xvi 1; 1 Cor. vii 15, &c.).

ἀδικία.text: ἀδικία, injustice, unrighteousness, hurt; sometimes in a Hebraistic genitive, equivalent to the adjective ἄδικος (e.g. Lk. xvi 8, xviii 6).

ᾅδης.text: ᾅδης (in LXX=Sheol), Hades, the unseen world, into which the spirits of all persons pass at death.

ἀθετέω.text: ἀθετέω, I annul, make of no effect, set aside, ignore, slight; I break faith with, Mk. vi 26.

ἀδύνατος.text: ἀδύνατος, (a) of persons, incapable (Ac. xiv 8, Rom. xv 1); (b) of things, impossible; τὸ ἀδύνατον, either the inability, or that which is impossible (Rom. viii 3).

ἀδόκιμος.text: ἀδόκιμος, failing to pass the test, unapproved, counterfeit.

αἴρω.text: αἴρω, (a) I raise, lift up; (b) I take away, remove.

αἷμα.text: αἷμα, blood (especially as shed): σὰρξ καὶ αἷμα (αἷμα καὶ σὰρξ), a Hebraistic expression for a human being, human beings, human nature.

αἰών.text: αἰών (from a root meaning life, especially long life, old age), an age, a cycle (of time), especially of the present age as contrasted with the future age, and of one of a series of ages stretching to infinity: ἀπ᾽ αἰῶνος, from the beginning of the present age, from the beginning of time, Lk. i 70, &c.: εἰς αἰῶνα (in saeculum, in aeternum, Ambros. expos. ps. cxviii 12 7 § 1): αἰῶνες αἰώνων, a Hebraistic expression, more emphatic than the simple αἰῶνες Gal. i 5, &c.

αἰτέω.text: αἰτέω, I ask, request, beg, petition: middle voice αἰτέομαι, I ask for myself (perhaps with entreaty).

αἰώνιος.text: αἰώνιος, (a) age-long, and, therefore, practically eternal, unending; (b) partaking of the character of that which lasts for an age, as contrasted with that which is brief and fleeting.

αἰτία.text: αἰτία, (a) a cause, reason; excuse; (b) a charge, accusation; (c) guilt; (d) relationship, matter, circumstances, case (= causa), Mt. xix 10.

ἀκολουθέω.text: ἀκολουθέω (takes the place of the old ἕπομαι), I accompany, attend.

ἀκάθαρτος.text: ἀκάθαρτος, unclean, impure: in reference to demons, spirits, Mt. x 1, &c.

ἀκοή.text: ἀκοή, (a) hearing, faculty of hearing; ear: in ἀκοῇ ἀκούειν (Mt. xiii 14, &c.), a Hebraistic (?) expression, the ἀκοῇ is emphatic; (b) report, rumour.

ἀκαταστασία.text: ἀκαταστασία, disturbance, upheaval, revolution, almost anarchy, first in the political, and thence in the moral sphere.

ἀκούω.text: ἀκούω, I hear, listen; in the passive, is heard, is reported: ἀκοῇ ἀκούειν, see ἀκοή.

ἀκροβυστία.text: ἀκροβυστία (a technical word of Jewish use, adapted from ἀκροποσθία [?]), foreskin, prepuce: used sometimes as a slang term by Jews, of Gentiles (Eph. ii 11).

ἀλήθεια.text: ἀλήθεια, truth, but not merely truth as spoken; truth of idea, reality, sincerity, truth in the moral sphere, straightforwardness: ἐπ᾽ ἀληθείας, really, truly.

ἀληθινός.text: ἀληθινός (less common than ἀληθής), true (lit. made of truth), real, genuine.

ἀληθής.text: ἀληθής, true in fact; hence more widely (see ἀλήθεια).

ἀλλά.text: ἀλλά (used very like πλήν), but; except, Mk. iv 22, Mt. xx 23; ἀλλ᾽ ἤ, except, 2 Cor. i 13; in Mk. vi 9 ἀλλά is probably a misrendering of an Aramaic word meaning and not.

ἄλλος.text: ἄλλος (alius), other, another (of more than two), different; see under ἕτερος; ὁ ἄλλος, the other (of two only), Mt. v 39, &c.; ἄλλοι ἄλλο τι . . . some—one thing, some—another thing.

ἀλλήλων.text: ἀλλήλων &c. (a reciprocal word = inter se, in uicem), one another.

ἀλλότριος.text: ἀλλότριος (alienus), belonging to another person, belonging to others.

ἁμαρτία.text: ἁμαρτία (error, a wrong state of mind or soul), a sin.

ἁμαρτωλός.text: ἁμαρτωλός, (a) sinning, sinful; (b) frequent as a translation of a contemptuous Aramaic word, with reference to particular classes despised by strict Jews, a sinner.

ἁμαρτάνω.text: ἁμαρτάνω, originally, I miss the mark; hence, (a) I make a mistake; (b) I sin, I commit a sin (against God); sometimes (Lk. xvii 4, Ac. xxv 8, &c.) the idea of sinning against a fellow-creature is present.

ἅμα.text: ἅμα, (a) adv. at the same time, therewith; (b) prep. along with, together with.

ἀμήν.text: ἀμήν (Hebr.), verily, truly: at the end of sentences may be paraphrased by So let it be!

ἀμπελών.text: ἀμπελών, a vineyard (-ών [=Lat. -etum] indicates ‘plantation of’, cf. ἐλαιών).

ἀμφότεροι.text: ἀμφότεροι, both (of two): in Ac. xix 16, xxiii 8, perhaps = all (of more than two); so in common speech and in Byzantine Greek.

ἄν.text: ἄν, (a) an untranslatable word (under the circumstances, in that case, anyhow), the general effect of which is to make a statement contingent, which would otherwise be definite: it is thus regularly used with the subjunctive mood: cf. ἕως ἄν, until such time as, ὃς ἄν, ὅστις ἄν, whosoever, ὅσοι ἄν, as many as . . . may, ὅπως ἄν, ὡς ἄν (1 Cor. xi 34, &c., not in 1 Cor. xii 2), that so; so, with the indicative past, in the apodosis of a conditional sentence, e.g. Mt. xi 21 ἂν . . . μετένοησαν, ‘would have repented’, where μετένοησαν alone would have meant ‘repented’; cf. also Mk. vii 11 (reading ὃ ἂν . . . ὠφελήθης); and with the optative (rare in N.T.), e.g. τί ἂν θέλοι, ‘how he would like’ (Lk. i 62), where τί θέλοι would be ‘how he might like’; (b) if (=Attic ἤν, ἐάν), e.g. John xii 32 (v.l.), xiii 20.
ἄν.note: μετένοησαν (twice) is accented thus on the page; transcribed as printed

ἀνά.text: ἀνά, prep. up; hence up along; ἀνὰ μέσον, in the middle: most commonly with a distributive force, e.g. ἀνὰ δηνάριον (Mt. xx 9), ‘a denarius each’, ἀνὰ δύο χιτῶνας (Lk. ix 3), ‘two tunics each’, ἀνὰ πεντήκοντα (Lk. ix 14), ‘in fifties’, ‘in groups of fifty’, ἀνὰ δύο (Lk. x 1), ‘two by two’ (where perhaps ἀνὰ δύο δύο, a mixed distributive, ought to be read).

ἀναβαίνω.text: ἀναβαίνω, I go up, mount, ascend.

ἀναγινώσκω.text: ἀναγινώσκω, I read aloud (in the scriptures, i.e. the Old Testament).

ἀναβλέπω.text: ἀναβλέπω, (a) I look up, e.g. Mt. xiv 19; (b) I recover my sight, e.g. Mt. xi 5.

ἀνάγω.text: ἀνάγω, (a) I lead up; (b) mid. and pass. I put to sea, set sail.

ἀνάγκη.text: ἀνάγκη, necessity, constraint, compulsion; ἔχω ἀνάγκην, I am obliged.

ἀναιρέω.text: ἀναιρέω, (a) I take up, e.g. Ac. vii 21; more often (b) I take away the life of, murder (2 Thess. ii 8, text doubtful).

ἀνάκειμαι.text: ἀνάκειμαι, I recline (especially at a dinner-table).

ἀνάθεμα.text: ἀνάθεμα (properly, a devoting to the vengeance of the infernal goddesses), a curse, a cursed thing. Distinguish from ἀνάθημα, q.v.

ἀνακρίνω.text: ἀνακρίνω, I examine, inquire into (judicially: see ἀνάκρισις); of the preliminary examination, preceding the trial proper: hence with derived applications.

ἀναλαμβάνω.text: ἀναλαμβάνω, (a) I take up, raise; (b) I pick up, 2 Tim. iv 11, or take on board, Ac. xx 13, 14; (c) I carry off, lead away, Ac. xxiii 31.

ἀναμιμνῄσκω.text: ἀναμιμνῄσκω, (a) act. I remind; (b) mid. or pass. I am reminded, remind myself, remember, recall.

ἀναπίπτω.text: ἀναπίπτω, I lie down, recline (at a dinner-table), I fall back upon (the breast of another person reclining at dinner).

ἀναπαύω.text: ἀναπαύω, (a) act. I make to rest, I give rest to; (b) mid. and pass. I rest, take my ease (see ἀνάπαυσις).

ἀναπληρόω.text: ἀναπληρόω, (a) I fill up, make up, complete the measure of, Phil. ii 30; (b) I fulfil, I carry out the commands (provisions, &c.) of, Mt. xiii 14, Gal. vi 2, &c.

ἀναχωρέω.text: ἀναχωρέω, (a) I return, Mt. ii 12; (b) I retire, depart (underlying idea perhaps of taking refuge from danger or of going into retirement).

ἀναστροφή.text: ἀναστροφή (conuersatio) (not in papyri, common in inscriptions), dealing with other men, going up and down among men, life, manner of life.

ἀνατολή.text: ἀνατολή, (a) rising of the sun; hence, (b) (sing. and plur.) the quarter whence the sun rises, the East.

ἀναστρέφω.text: ἀναστρέφω, (a) I overturn, turn upside down, John ii 15 (text doubtful); (b) I return, Ac. v 22, xv 16 (in a Hebraistic idiom, where the verb means little more than the adverb again); (c) mid. and pass. (conuersari) I conduct (behave) myself, live (with reference to the manner of life, especially in a moral and religious aspect), Mt. xvii 22 (text doubtful), &c., often with ἐν and a noun indicating condition or circumstances.

ἀναφέρω.text: ἀναφέρω, (a) I carry up, lead up; (b) I offer up (on a high altar) as a sacrifice, I offer up to God on high.

ἄνεμος.text: ἄνεμος, wind (literally, and in Eph. iv 14 metaph.): in the sense quarter of the heaven, cardinal point, as both Greeks and Romans habitually defined the quarters of the heaven by the winds which came from those quarters, Mt. xxiv 31 (Mk. xiii 27).

ἀνέγκλητος.text: ἀνέγκλητος, irreproachable (especially in private life), blameless.

ἄνεσις.text: ἄνεσις (opposite of θλῖψις, lit. loosening, relaxing), (a) relief, remission, indulgence, freedom, Ac. xxiv 23; (b) rest.

ἄνθρωπος.text: ἄνθρωπος, a human being: υἱὸς ἀνθρώπου, notable because of the singular (rather than the plural ἀνθρώπων), a Hebraistic expression of a somewhat frequent type (see under υἱός), indicating a human being with all the characteristics of a human being (ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου, a Messianic title especially favoured by our Lord for this very reason).

ἀνήρ.text: ἀνήρ (uir), a male human being, a man (contrast ἄνθρωπος); often in addresses, at the beginning of speeches = Gentlemen; a husband.

ἀνέχομαι.text: ἀνέχομαι, I endure (in 2 Thess. i 4, and Mt. vi 24=Lk. xvi 13, text doubtful).

ἀνθίστημι.text: ἀνθίστημι, only in intransitive tenses of active, and in all tenses of the middle or passive, I take a stand against, oppose, resist.

ἀνθρώπινος.text: ἀνθρώπινος, belonging to human beings (especially as contrasted with God), human (as contrasted with divine): perhaps moderate, Rom. vi 19, 1 Cor. x 13.

ἀνίστημι.text: ἀνίστημι, I raise up, set up: only the fut. ἀναστήσω and the 1 aor. ἀνέστησα are used in this transitive sense in the N.T.; much more frequent are the middle voice and the 2 aor. of the active in the intr. sense I rise, especially ἐκ νεκρῶν, from among (the) dead bodies, dead persons, the dead.

ἀνομία.text: ἀνομία, lawlessness; especially disobedience to the divine law, sin.

ἀντί.text: ἀντί (originally local, in front of, opposite), (a) instead of, in return for, in exchange for, as a substitute for; λύτρον ἀντὶ πολλῶν Mk. x 45 (=Mt. xx 28), a ransom to buy the many, for the many; cf. Heb. xii 16 and ἀντίλυτρον; (b) ἀντὶ ἐμοῦ, on my behalf, Mt. xvii 27; (c) ἀνθ᾽ ὧν (literally, in return for which things) has become a conjunction, wherefore, because.

ἄνομος.text: ἄνομος, lawless, disobedient to the law of God, sinful; illegal: ἄνομος θεοῦ=ἄνευ νόμου θεοῦ, 1 Cor. ix 21.

ἀντίκειμαι.text: ἀντίκειμαι (used as a passive for ἀντιτίθημι, just as κεῖμαι is a passive for τίθημι), I resist, oppose.

ἀντίδικος.text: ἀντίδικος (aduersarius), an opponent (in a lawsuit): probably so even in 1 Pet. v 8.

ἀντιτάσσομαι.text: ἀντιτάσσομαι, I range myself against, resist (the attack of).

ἀπαγγέλλω.text: ἀπαγγέλλω, I report (from one place to another), I bring a report, I announce.

ἄνωθεν.text: ἄνωθεν, (a) from above, sometimes strengthened by ἀπό, from heaven (locally and spiritually); (b) from the beginning, from their origin (source), from of old, Lk. i 3, Ac. xxvi 5, Gal. iv 9, James i 17; (c) again (the meaning taken out of Jesus' words by Nicodemus, John iii 4, where δεύτερον is his paraphrase of ἄνωθεν (iii 3)).

ἀξιόω.text: ἀξιόω, I account or treat as worthy.

ἀξίως.text: ἀξίως, worthily; in a manner worthy of . . . .

ἅπας.text: ἅπας, all, whole (cf. πᾶς). It is rather a literary word and is used by preference after consonants.

ἀπάγω.text: ἀπάγω, I lead away, [for example (=duco) I lead away to execution, Ac. xii 19]; hence, in the moral sphere, 1 Cor. xii 2; also, of a road leading to a place.

ἀπαρνέομαι.text: ἀπαρνέομαι, I deny, disown, repudiate (either another person or myself).

ἀπαρχή.text: ἀπαρχή, first-fruits, the earliest crop of the year; hence also metaph., for example, of the earliest converts in a district. There is evidence in favour of rendering in some passages merely by sacrifice, gift.

ἀπειθέω.text: ἀπειθέω, I disobey, I rebel, I am disloyal.

ἀπεκδέχομαι.text: ἀπεκδέχομαι (rare), I expect eagerly, I wait for eagerly.

ἄπειμι.text: ἄπειμι (B), I shall go away, I go away (only Ac. xvii 10).

ἀπείθεια.text: ἀπείθεια, disobedience, rebellion, contumacy: for υἱοὶ τῆς ἀπειθείας, see υἱός.

ἀπό.text: ἀπό, with nouns or adverbs, from, (as distinguished from ἐκ) = from the outside of, away from: ἀπ’ ἀγορᾶς, fresh from market, Mk. vii 4, ἀπ’ ἀγροῦ, fresh from the country, Mk. xv 21: Rev. i 4, construction is peculiar: οἱ ἀπὸ τῆς Ἰταλίας, those who are in (?) Italy, Heb. xiii 24: φοβεῖσθαι ἀπό, see φοβέομαι: by (expressing agent), e.g. Lk. viii 43: = gen. of material, Mt. iii 4, xxvii 21.

ἀπέρχομαι.text: ἀπέρχομαι, I go away from (a place).

ἄπιστος.text: ἄπιστος, unbelieving, incredulous; unchristian: sometimes substantivally, unbeliever.

ἀπέχω.text: ἀπέχω, (trans.) I have received (payment), a formula of receipts: so prob. also in Mk. xiv 41, ὁ Ἰούδας being understood as subject (there is hardly any other example in Greek of the meaning it is sufficient, but see Field ad loc.); (intrans.) I am away (distant) (from), of places and objects; (middle voice) I keep myself away (from), I refrain (from), I abstain (from).

ἀπιστέω.text: ἀπιστέω, (a) I am unfaithful; (b) I disbelieve.

ἀποδίδωμι.text: ἀποδίδωμι (reddo), (a) I give back, return, restore; (b) I give, render, as due; (c) middle, I sell, Ac. v 8, &c.

ἀποδοκιμάζω.text: ἀποδοκιμάζω, I reject after testing (examination), I disqualify.

ἀποδέχομαι.text: ἀποδέχομαι, I receive, welcome, entertain (with hospitality); hence metaph. Ac. ii 41, xxiv 3.
ἀποδέχομαι.note: Mark after headword looks like a semicolon on the image (probably a comma with a speck above it); transcribed as a comma.

ἀποκρίνομαι.text: ἀποκρίνομαι, I answer (either a spoken or an unspoken question): ἀπεκρίθην, &c. (absent from papyri after second cent. B.C.), are borrowed by N.T. from LXX: ἀπεκρινάμην, I uttered solemnly, Lk. iii 16, John v 17, 19, Ac. iii 12; I replied in a court of law, Mt. xxvii 12, Mk. xiv 61, Lk. xxiii 9 (cf. John v 11 v.l.).

ἀποθνῄσκω.text: ἀποθνῄσκω, I am dying (= obsolete θνῄσκω), Lk. viii 42, 2 Cor. vi 9, Heb. xi 21: aor. ἀποθανεῖν, to die: the present is frequentative in 1 Cor. xv 22, Heb. vii 8, x 28, Rev. xiv 13 (different individuals), iterative in 1 Cor. xv 31 (same person), equivalent to the future, John xxi 23, 1 Cor. xv 32.

ἀποκτείνω.text: ἀποκτείνω, ἀποκτέννω, ἀποκτεννύω (absent from papyri of N.T. times), I kill.

ἀποκαλύπτω.text: ἀποκαλύπτω, I unveil, reveal (correlative to μυστήριον, secret).

ἀποκαθίστημι.text: ἀποκαθιστάνω, ἀποκαθίστημι, I set up again, I restore to its original position or condition; hence, I restore, give back.

ἀποθήκη.text: ἀποθήκη, a store-house, store-room for food-stuffs, a barn.

ἀποκόπτω.text: ἀποκόπτω, (a) I cut off, I cut loose; (b) I emasculate, castrate (Gal. v 12, where middle = passive, probably).

ἀπόλλυμι.text: ἀπόλλυμι, (a) I destroy; (b) I lose: (mid.) I am perishing (the resultant death being viewed as certain).

ἀπολύω.text: ἀπολύω (dimitto), I let loose, set free, release, permit to depart: middle, I withdraw myself, depart, Ac. xxviii 25.

ἀπολογέομαι.text: ἀπολογέομαι, I give a defence, I defend myself (especially in a law court): it can take an obj. of what is said in defence.

ἀπολύτρωσις.text: ἀπολύτρωσις, ransoming, deliverance, liberation (from captivity), ransoming away, emancipation, manumission (of a slave by his master) (the idea of payment, though originally present, seems wholly to have disappeared in N.T.).

ἀπολογία.text: ἀπολογία, a defence (particularly in a law court).

ἀποστέλλω.text: ἀποστέλλω, I send away, commission; I put forth, Mk. iv 29.

ἀπόστολος.text: ἀπόστολος, a messenger, an envoy, a delegate, one commissioned by another to represent him in some way, especially a man sent out by Jesus Christ Himself to preach the Gospel, an apostle.

ἀποτίθημι.text: ἀποτίθεμαι, I put off (away), cast off (away) from myself; hence, I put, store (in).

ἀπορέω.text: ἀπορέω (lit. I lose the way), esp. in mid., I am in difficulties, I am at my wits' end.

ἀποτάσσομαι.text: ἀποτάσσομαι, I give parting instructions; I say farewell (good-bye), I take leave.

ἅπτω.text: ἅπτω, (a) act. I light, kindle; (b) mid. c. gen. I lay hold of, I cling to (eagerly).

ἀποφέρω.text: ἀποφέρω, I carry, bear away (sometimes with violence, as Mk. xv 1).

ἄρα.text: ἄρα, an inferential particle, then, therefore: found also in combination with other particles, such as γε and οὖν, &c.; εἰ ἄρα (si forte), if perchance, Mk. xi 13, &c.

ἀργύριον.text: ἀργύριον, a piece of silver-money (except 1 Cor. iii 12, where silver).

ἀρέσκω.text: ἀρέσκω, I please, with the idea of willing service rendered to others; hence almost I serve.

ἀργός.text: ἀργός, (a) idle, lazy; (b) thoughtless, Mt. xii 36.

ἀρετή.text: ἀρετή (uirtus, a word of wide significance in non-Christian ethics), excellence, particularly moral excellence; manifestation of power, 2 Pet. i 3.

ἀρνέομαι.text: ἀρνέομαι, (a) I deny (a statement); (b) I repudiate (a person, or belief).

ἀρνίον.text: ἀρνίον (originally, a little lamb, but diminutive force was lost), a lamb: see ἀρήν.

ἀρχή.text: ἀρχή, (a) rule (kingly or magisterial); (b) plur., in a quasi-personal sense, almost rulers, magistrates, Tit. iii 1; (c) beginning: in the very difficult John viii 25 τὴν ἀρχήν would naturally mean originally, but the passage is not yet explained.

ἄρτι.text: ἄρτι (of present time), now, just now.

ἁρπάζω.text: ἁρπάζω, I seize, snatch, obtain by robbery.

ἀρχαῖος.text: ἀρχαῖος, original, primitive; ancient, Mt. v 21, &c.

ἄρχω.text: ἄρχω, (1) act. c. gen. I rule; (2) mid. I begin; sometimes in this sense the word is otiose, being merely an imitation of O.T. language or a literal translation of Hebrew or Aramaic, e.g. repeatedly in the Synoptic Gospels, and particularly in Mk., Lk. iii 8, &c.

ἄρχων.text: ἄρχων, a ruler, governor, leader, leading man; with the Jews, an official member (a member of the executive) of the γερουσία.

ἀρχισυνάγωγος.text: ἀρχισυνάγωγος, a leader of the synagogue, a leading man (or woman) connected with the synagogue: sometimes there was only one, and the name was in some cases merely honorary.

ἀσπάζομαι.text: ἀσπάζομαι (saluto, a term regularly used at the end of a letter), I greet, salute; I pay my respects to, Ac. xxv 13.

ἀσθενέω.text: ἀσθενέω, I am weak (physically: then morally), I am sick.

ἀσθενής.text: ἀσθενής (lit. not strong), (a) weak (physically, or morally); (b) ill.

ἀσθένεια.text: ἀσθένεια, want of strength, weakness, illness.

ἀσπασμός.text: ἀσπασμός (very rare in papyri), a greeting, salutation.

ἀσύνετος.text: ἀσύνετος (insipiens, non intellegens, Ambros. expos. in ps. cxviii 20 55 § 2), unintelligent, without wisdom, unwise, undiscerning (implying probably moral defect, like ἀμαθής sometimes in classical Greek).
ἀσύνετος.note: "20" in the Ambrose reference is printed in a heavier type than the surrounding figures; transcribed as printed.

αὐξάνω.text: αὐξάνω (αὔξω), (a) tr. (augeo) I cause to increase; (b) intr. (cresco) I increase, grow; with cogn. acc. Col. ii 19.

ἀτενίζω.text: ἀτενίζω, I direct my gaze, I look steadily.

αὐλή.text: αὐλή, court-yard, fore-court; but it may be understood as palace, house, e.g. Mt. xxvi 3.

ἀτιμάζω.text: ἀτιμάζω, I disgrace, treat disgracefully, dishonour, insult; I despise.

αὐτός.text: αὐτός (fem. αὐτή, neut. αὐτό), (a) he, &c.; (b) self; e.g. αὐτός ὁ, &c. (ipse ille), the very, but often weakened to mean simply that; αὐτός = αὐτόματος, of his own accord, John xvi 27; (c) ὁ αὐτὸς (idem), &c., the same. Parts of αὐτός are sometimes added pleonastically to the relative pronoun (colloquial) (where the usage is not due to inferior culture, it is due to translation-Greek), cf. Mk. vii 25; αὐτοῦ, adv., there; ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό, κατὰ τὸ αὐτό, together.

ἄφεσις.text: ἄφεσις (from ἀφίημι) (remissio), a sending away, a letting go, a release; hence (cf. in inscriptions, remission from debt or punishment), remission, forgiveness.

ἀφανίζω.text: ἀφανίζω, I cause to disappear, hide, remove; I disfigure (probably by leaving unwashed for a long period), Mt. vi 16.

ἀφίημι.text: ἀφίημι, (a) I send away; (b) I let go or away, release, permit to depart; (c) I remit, forgive; (d) I permit, followed by the subjunctive with (or without) ἵνα, or with acc. obj. and infin.; ἄφες ἐκβάλω (Mt. vii 4 = Lk. vi 42), let me (allow me to) cast out: so also Mt. xxvii 49 = Mk. xv 36, John xii 7.

ἀφίσταμαι.text: ἀφίστημι (a) 1 aor. tr. I made to stand away, I drew away, Ac. v 37; I repelled; (b) other tenses of act., and mid. I take up a position away from, I withdraw from, I leave.

ἀφορίζω.text: ἀφορίζω, I rail off, I separate, I place apart.

ἄχρι.text: ἄχρι, ἄχρις, as far as, up to, until; ἄχρι τοῦ νῦν = adhuc; ἄχρι οὗ (with or without ἄν) with the subjunctive, until.

βάλλω.text: βάλλω (a) I cast, throw; intr. I rush, Ac. xxvii 14; (b) often, in the weaker sense (cf. mitto), I place, put, drop; βεβλημένος, lying in bed, Mt. viii 14.

βαπτίζω.text: βαπτίζω, lit. I dip, submerge, but specifically of ceremonial dipping (whether immersion or affusion), I baptize; when the preposition εἰς with a noun in the accus. follows, it appears to indicate that through this ceremony the baptized person becomes the property of the person indicated after εἰς: met. Mk. x 38.

βάπτισμα.text: βάπτισμα, a dipping, a baptism: c. gen. μετανοίας, belonging to a change of mental attitude, sign of a change of mental attitude.

βαπτιστής.text: βαπτιστής, the baptizer, the baptist, epithet used only of John, the son of Zechariah and Elizabeth, forerunner of Jesus.

βασιλεία.text: βασιλεία, kingship, sovereignty, authority, rule, especially of God, both in the world, and in the hearts of men; hence kingdom, in the concrete sense; ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν perhaps always signifies the coming kingdom, but ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ is wider.

βασανίζω.note: Headword is printed βασάνιζω (accent on the second alpha, a misprint for βασανίζω); transcribed as printed.

βασιλεύς.text: βασιλεύς, a king, but in some passages, as 1 Pet. ii 17, clearly to be translated emperor: ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν βασιλέων (βασιλευόντων), the King of Kings, an oriental type of phrase, used for the Persian king as overlord of other kings, and in scripture of God.

βαστάζω.text: βαστάζω, (a) I carry, bear; (b) I carry (take) away, Mt. iii 11, John xx 15; I pilfer, John xii 6.

βασιλεύω.text: βασιλεύω, (a) I rule, reign; (b) I reign over, c. gen.

βέβηλος.text: βέβηλος, profane, secular; unspiritual, godless, worldly, Heb. xii 16.

βασιλικός.text: βασιλικός, connected with a king, royal, regal; in James ii 8 βασιλικὸς νόμος, a supreme law is referred to, the more important parts of the law: substantivally (a) an officer in the service of the king (Herod Antipas), John iv 46, 49; (b) ἡ βασιλικὴ (sc. χώρα), the king's country, Ac. xii 20.

βιβλίον.text: βιβλίον (libellus, originally a diminutive), a papyrus roll: ἀποστασίου, document of divorce, handed by the husband to the wife whom he divorces: ζωῆς, of life, preserved in heaven and containing the names of those who share in [eternal] life.

βλασφημέω.text: βλασφημέω, I speak evil against, I use abusive or scurrilous language about (God or men).

βῆμα.text: βῆμα (from root of ἔβην, I went), (a) βῆμα ποδός, the space covered by a step of the foot; (b) tribunal.

βίβλος.text: βίβλος (liber), a papyrus roll, with a sacred connotation: ζωῆς, see βιβλίον, which had almost ousted it.

βίος.text: βίος (uictus), (a) life; (b) manner of life; livelihood.

βλέπω.text: βλέπω (primarily physical), I look, see; βλέποντες βλέψετε, Hebraistic; βλέπειν ἀπό, to look away from, to beware of; βλέπειν μή, to take care lest; βλέπειν πῶς, to take care how: almost I find, Rom. vii 23 (cf. 21).

βρῶσις.text: βρῶσις, (a) (abstr.) eating; (b) food; a meal, Heb. xii 16; (c) rust.

γενεά.text: γενεά, a generation: in combination with another γενεά, or with αἰών, practically indicates infinity of time.

γαμέω.text: γαμέω, I marry, used of either sex.

γέ.text: γε, an enclitic, emphasizing particle (quidem), at least, indeed, really, but generally too subtle to be represented in English.
γέ.note: Printed headword is unaccented enclitic γε.

γάμος.text: γάμος, a marriage, wedding, wedding-ceremony: γάμοι (plur.), a wedding-feast.

γέεννα.text: γέεννα (Aram.), gehenna, and originally gē ben hinnōm name of a valley or cavity near Jerusalem, Jer. vii 31, 2 Kings xxiii 10, a place underneath the earth, a place of punishment (retributive or purificatory) for evil.

γίνομαι.text: γίνομαι, I come into being, am born, John viii 58, Gal. iv 4, &c.: I become, come about, happen. (In aorist ἐγένετο over-used by Luke, to give Hebraistic colouring, in various constructions: (1) ἐγένετο ἦλθεν, (2) ἐγένετο καὶ ἦλθεν, (3) ἐγένετο ἐλθεῖν (the latest of the three and non-Hebraistic).)

γεννάω.text: γεννάω, I beget (of the male), more rarely (e.g. Lk. i 13), (of the female) I bring forth.

γεωργός.text: γεωργός, a worker of the soil, husbandman, farmer, farm-labourer.

γένημα.text: γένημα (from γίνομαι), of vegetable, never of animal, products (contrast γέννημα), fruit, crop, produce of the earth.

γινώσκω.text: γινώσκω, I am taking in knowledge, come to know, learn: aor. I ascertained, realized, but not in John xvii 25, 2 Tim. ii 19.

γλῶσσα.text: γλῶσσα, (a) tongue, especially as an organ of speech; (b) tongue, language; (c) also, usually in the plural, for the unintelligible sounds uttered in spiritual ecstasy.

γυνή.text: γυνή, a (married) woman, a wife: so even in Mt. v 28: voc. γύναι, Lk. xxii 57, John ii 4, my lady.

γράφω.text: γράφω, I write: γέγραπται, it is written, it stands written (in the scriptures of the Old Testament: so in ordinary life, a formula introducing an unalterable agreement): = προγράφω, Rom. xv 4.

γραμματεύς.text: γραμματεύς, (a) in Jerusalem, a scribe, one learned in the Jewish Law, a religious teacher; (b) at Ephesus, the town-clerk, the secretary of the city, Ac. xix 35.

γραφή.text: γραφή, (a) a writing; (b) a passage of scripture: plur. αἱ γραφαί, the scriptures (of the Old Testament, and in 2 Pet. iii 16 also of the New).

γρηγορέω.text: γρηγορέω (uigilo), (a) I am awake (in the night), watch; (b) I am watchful, on the alert.

γυμνός.text: γυμνός, rarely stark-naked, generally wearing only the under-garment (χιτών), see γυμνιτεύω; γυμνὸς κόκκος, a simple seed, a seed per se.

γράμμα.text: γράμμα (littera), a letter of the alphabet; collectively, written (revelation), Rom. ii 27: γράμματα (litterae), writings, (a) a written document, Lk. xvi 6, 7; a letter, an epistle, Ac. xxviii 21; (b) writings, literature, John v 47, vii 15, Ac. xxvi 24, 2 Tim. iii 15.

δαιμονίζομαι.text: δαιμονίζομαι, I am under the power of an evil-spirit or demon.

δάκρυον.note: Printed headword is the double form δάκρυ, δάκρυον.

δέ.text: δέ (autem), a weak adversative particle, generally placed second in its clause, but, on the other hand: and. See μέν.

δείκνυμι.text: δείκνυμι, δεικνύω, I point out, show.

δέησις.text: δέησις, a requesting, a begging, request.

δεῖπνον.text: δεῖπνον, a dinner, an afternoon or evening meal.

δεξιός.text: δεξιός, on the right hand, right hand, right.

δεύτερος.text: δεύτερος, second: (τὸ) δεύτερον is used adverbially, in the second place, for the second time.

δέσμιος.text: δέσμιος, bound, captive, in chains; sometimes substantivally prisoner, captive.

δεσμός.text: δεσμός, plur. sometimes δεσμά, a bond, chain; in Ac. xxiii 29, xxvi 31 (= uincula), the reference is to the form of ‘capital’ punishment involving loss of freedom and work in chains in the quarries.

δεῦτε.text: δεῦτε (plur. of δεῦρο), come hither, come, hither, an exclamatory word.

δεσπότης.text: δεσπότης, a master, particularly a master and owner of slaves, lord.

διά.text: διά, (a) c. gen. through: throughout (διὰ παντός, always); by the instrumentality of: denoting mediate and not original authorship, e.g. Mt. i 22, John i 3, 1 Cor. viii 6; (b) c. acc. through, Lk. xvii 11 (?); on account of, by reason of, for the sake of, because of.

διάβολος.text: διάβολος (adj. used oftener as noun), slanderous (1 Tim. iii 11, 2 Tim. iii 3, Tit. ii 3); almost always ὁ Διάβολος, the Slanderer (par excellence), the Devil.

δηνάριον.text: δηνάριον, a denarius, a small Roman silver coin, weighing in Nero's time 53 grs. Its value and purchasing power varied from time to time.

διακονέω.text: διακονέω (ministro), I wait at table (particularly of a slave who pours out wine to the guests); I serve (generally).

διακονία.text: διακονία (ministerium), waiting at table; in a wider sense, service, ministration.

διαθήκη.text: διαθήκη, (a) = συνθήκη, a covenant between two parties; (b) (the ordinary, everyday sense [found a countless number of times in papyri]) a will, testament, Gal. iii 15, 17, Heb. ix 16. See my Text and Canon, p. 157, n. 2.

διάκονος.text: διάκονος (minister), a waiter, servant: then of any one who performs any service, an administrator, &c.

διακρίνω.text: διακρίνω, I separate, distinguish, discern one thing from another; διακρίνομαι, I doubt, hesitate, waver.

διαμαρτύρομαι.text: διαμαρτύρομαι, I give solemn evidence, I testify (declare) solemnly.

διαλογισμός.text: διαλογισμός, a calculation, reasoning, thought, movement of thought, deliberation, plotting.

διαλέγομαι.text: διαλέγομαι, I converse, Mk. ix 34; elsewhere, I address, preach, lecture.

διάνοια.text: διάνοια (process of reasoning in Plato), understanding, intellect, mind.

διαμερίζω.text: διαμερίζω, I divide up into parts, break up; I distribute.

διαφέρω.text: διαφέρω, (a) tr. I carry through, hither and thither; (b) intr. I am different, I differ, sometimes c. gen.: hence c. gen. I surpass, I excel.

διατρίβω.text: διατρίβω, I tarry, continue, stay in a place.

διαστέλλομαι.text: διαστέλλομαι, I give a commission (instructions), I order.

διασῴζω.text: διασῴζω, I save (rescue) through (some danger): διασ. πρός (Ac. xxiii 34), I bring safely to, so διεσώθησαν εἰς (1 Pet. iii 20), escaped into.

διατίθεμαι.text: διατίθεμαι, (a) I appoint, make (of a covenant); (b) I make (a will) (regular in papyri), Heb. ix 16, 17.

δίδωμι.text: δίδωμι, I offer, give; elliptically used Rev. ii 23: (Hebraistic = τίθημι), I put, place, Rev. iii 8.

διέρχομαι.text: διέρχομαι, I go (come, journey) all the way through: in Ac. seems frequently to imply, I itinerate, evangelize as I go.

δικαιοσύνη.text: δικαιοσύνη (usually if not always in Jewish atmosphere), justice, justness: righteousness (cf. δίκαιος): δικαιοσύνη θεοῦ strictly, righteousness of which God is the source or author, but practically, a divine righteousness and equivalent to βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ.

δίκαιος.text: δίκαιος, just; especially, just in the eyes of God, righteous: οἱ δίκαιοι in Mt. the elect (a Jewish idea): κρίνω τὸ δίκαιον, I give just judgement, Lk. xii 57.

διό.text: διό (= δι’ ὅ, on account of which thing), wherefore.

δικαιόω.text: δικαιόω, I make δίκαιος (righteous), I defend the cause of, plead for the righteousness (innocence) of, I acquit, justify; hence, I regard as δίκαιος (righteous).

δικαίωμα.text: δικαίωμα, (an argument, a pièce justificative, hence) a thing pronounced (by God) to be δίκαιος (just, the right); or the restoration of a criminal, a fresh chance given him; a righteous deed (e.g. Rom. v 18).

δοκέω.text: δοκέω (uideor), I seem, am thought; δοκεῖ impers. c. dat. (placet), it seems good, it is resolved by.

διώκω.text: διώκω, I pursue; hence, I persecute.

διότι.text: διότι (= διὰ ὅ τι), wherefore; = ὅτι Rom. viii 21 (v.l.).

δοκιμάζω.text: δοκιμάζω, I put to the test, I prove, examine: in Rom. ii 18, Phil. i 10 either I distinguish by testing, or, more probably, I approve after testing: I think fit, Rom. i 28.

δόξα.text: δόξα, glory, an especially divine quality, the unspoken manifestation of God; in James ii 1 it is in apposition to Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, and is personified (cf. 1 Cor. ii 8, Ac. vii 2, and the Shekinah of Targums and post-canonical Jewish writings).
δόξα.note: Hyphen in post-canonical falls at a line break; kept as a real hyphen.

δοῦλος.text: δοῦλος, (a) (as adj.) enslaved, subject; (b) (as noun) a (male) slave.

δοξάζω.text: δοξάζω, I glorify, bestow glory on: τὸν θεόν, I acknowledge the glory of God.

δουλεύω.text: δουλεύω, I serve as a slave, I am a slave.

δύναμαι.text: δύναμαι, (a) I am powerful, I have (the) power; (b) I am able, I can.

δύο.text: δύο, two: δυὸ δυό, two by two; ἀνὰ (κατὰ) δύο, two by two: ἀνὰ δύο δύο in some MSS of Luke x 3 is a mistaken fusion of the two phrases.
δύο.note: Accents δυὸ δυό and (κατὰ) are as printed.

δύναμις.text: δύναμις, (a) physical power, force, might; (b) in plur., powerful deeds, deeds showing (physical) power, marvellous works.

δώδεκα.text: δώδεκα, twelve: οἱ δώδεκα, the usual way in which the Twelve disciples of Jesus are referred to.

δυνατός.text: δυνατός, (a) of persons, powerful, able; (b) of things, possible.

δωρεά.text: δωρεά, a (free) gift, a gift (without repayment).

ἑαυτοῦ.text: ἑαυτοῦ, &c., self, selves; for all three persons, singular (not first person) and plural, according to context, ourselves; yourself, yourselves; himself, herself, itself, themselves.

ἐάν.text: ἐάν, (a) introducing a clause, if, with subjunctive, but 1 Thess. iii 8, 1 John v 15 have the indicative; (b) (an usage beginning about 133 B.C.) within a clause, modifying, generalizing, ὅς, ὅστις, ὅσος, ὁσάκις, ὅπου, οὗ, exactly as ἄν does in Attic Greek: thus ὅς = who, ὅς ἐάν, whosoever, &c.

δωρεάν.text: δωρεάν (acc. of δωρεά used as adv., cf. gratis abl. plur. of gratia), as a free gift, without payment, freely, gratis.

ἐγώ.text: ἐγώ, I: τί ἐμοὶ (ἡμῖν) καὶ σοί; quid mihi (nobis) tecum? What have I (we) to do with thee?, but in John ii 4 ἐμοὶ καὶ σοί may be simply equal to ἡμῖν; τὸ (τὰ) κατ’ ἐμέ, so far as I am concerned: in letters ἡμεῖς often alternates with ἐγώ without real difference of meaning.

ἐγείρω.text: ἐγείρω, (a) I wake, arouse; (b) I raise up; intr. in imperative, ἔγειρε, ἐγείρεσθε, wake up!: passive sometimes = I rise, e.g. Mk. xvi 6.

ἐγκαλέω.text: ἐγκαλέω, I bring a charge against.

εἰ.text: εἰ, if: but in strong statements, approaching oaths in character, and as the first word in an interrogative clause, it is probably a mere graphic equivalent, first appearing second century B.C., of ἦ [and should be written εἶ], and in the former case = verily, indeed, assuredly (sometimes negative [Semitic], assuredly not, Mk. viii 12, Heb. iii 11), while in the latter it is merely a particle asking a question. [The Latin translators, however, rendered interrogative εἶ by si.] εἰ μή (nisi); but only, e.g. Lk. iv 26 f., John xv 4, Ac. xxvii 22, Rev. xxi 27; in Mk. vi 8 probably due to a misreading of an Aramaic word = and not: εἰ δὲ μή, εἰ δὲ μήγε (Aramaism?), (alioqui, si minus, sin autem, &c.), otherwise: εἴπερ (= εἴ περ) a more emphatic εἰ, if indeed.

ἔθνος.text: ἔθνος (originally, a rustic or village people as opposed to those dwelling in organized cities or πόλεις), a race, people (usually outside the privileged Jewish people, but also sometimes in the singular for it) (sometimes = the inhabitants of a Roman province): τὰ ἔθνη (gentes), the nations outside Judaism, the Gentiles.

εἴδωλον.text: εἴδωλον (simulacrum), an image of a god.

εἰδωλολάτρης.text: εἰδωλολάτρης, a server (worshipper) of an image (of a god).

εἶδος.text: εἶδος, visible form, shape, appearance, outward show; in 1 Thess. v 22 = kind, species, class.

εἰμί.text: εἰμί, I am, exist. Note periphrasis with participles, the special frequency of which in the imperfect is due to the Aramaic basis of the language. ὁ ἦν ungrammatically, in Rev., where an aor. pcpl. would be expected.

εἰς.text: εἰς, (a) into; till; for; (b) εἰς τό c. infin. generally final, but also expressing tendency, result, e.g. Rom. xii 3, 2 Cor. viii 6, Gal. iii 17, content of command or entreaty, e.g. 1 Thess. ii 12, or simply = explanatory infinitive, 1 Thess. iv 9; (c) encroaches on ἐν and = in, e.g. John i 18, Ac. vii 12, 2 Cor. xi 10, 1 John v 8: εἰς ἑκατόν, &c., a hundredfold.

εἷς.text: εἷς, one; καθ’ εἷς, each single one, one by one: sometimes no whit different from τις (Mk. xiv 10), and sometimes too = πρῶτος, first.

εἰρήνη.text: εἰρήνη, peace, undisturbedness: invocation of peace a common Jewish farewell (Mk. v 34, &c.), in the Hebraistic sense of the health (welfare) of an individual.

εἰσάγω.text: εἰσάγω, I lead in, bring in.

ἐκ.text: ἐκ, ἐξ, from out, out from among, from, suggesting from the interior outwards; ἐξ Ἑβραίων, descended from Hebrews, Phil. iii 5: with gen. of price, Mt. xx 2, Ac. i 18; in partitive phrase, as subject of sentence, John xvi 17; cf. the periphrasis οἱ ἐξ ἐριθείας, Rom. ii 8.

ἐκβάλλω.text: ἐκβάλλω, I throw (cast, put) out; I banish, Gal. iv 30, 3 John 10; I bring forth, I produce, Mt. xii 35.

ἕκαστος.text: ἕκαστος (quisque), each (of more than two); εἷς ἕκαστος, each individual; plur. ἕκαστοι, &c., each class, group.

εἰσπορεύομαι.text: εἰσπορεύομαι, I journey in(to), I go in(to).

ἑκατοντάρχης.text: ἑκατοντάρχης (-ος) (centurio, see κεντουρίων), a centurion of the Roman army.

ἑκατόν.text: ἑκατόν, a hundred; εἰς ἑκατόν, see εἰς.

εἶτα.text: εἶτα, then, thereafter, next (marking a fresh stage).

ἐκεῖνος.text: ἐκεῖνος (ille), that, yonder (of what is distant, or great): in 1 John usually = Christ.

ἐκκλησία.text: ἐκκλησία, (literally, a calling out; then) an assembly, meeting of assembly, Ac. xix 39; (a) a community, congregation, church, society (first used in LXX for the congregation of Israel), the assembly of Christians in one city or community; in Mt. xvi 18, xviii 17 the body of Palestinian adherents of the Messiah is intended; (b) much more rarely, in a developed sense, especially with ὅλη, the Church (the whole body of Christians in the world).

ἐκδίκησις.text: ἐκδίκησις, (a) defence, avenging, vindication, vengeance; (b) full (complete) punishment, 2 Thess. i 8, 1 Pet. ii 14.

ἐκδικέω.text: ἐκδικέω, I give justice over, defend, avenge, vindicate.

ἐκλεκτός.text: ἐκλεκτός, chosen out, selected, sometimes as substantive, of those chosen out by God for the rendering of special service to Him (of the Hebrew race, particular Hebrews, the Messiah, and the Christians): an adj. in 2 John 1, 13.

ἐκλέγομαι.text: ἐκλέγομαι, I pick out for myself, I choose.

ἐκλογή.text: ἐκλογή, choosing out, selecting, choice (by God): in Ac. ix 15 a Hebraistic genitive, equivalent to ἐκλεκτόν.

ἐκλύομαι.text: ἐκλύομαι, I am unstrung, become weak, fail.

ἐκπορεύομαι.text: ἐκπορεύομαι, I journey out; I come forth.

ἐκπίπτω.text: ἐκπίπτω, I fall out, I fall off, I fall away: hence, in nautical language, I fall off from the straight course: of flowers, I fade away, wither away.

ἔκστασις.text: ἔκστασις (properly, distraction or disturbance of mind caused by a shock), bewilderment.

ἐκχέω.text: ἐκχέω, I pour out (liquid or solid), I shed. See ἐκχύννω.

ἐλάχιστος.text: ἐλάχιστος, least, smallest (Mt., 1 Cor. xv 9), but perhaps oftener in the weaker sense, very little, very small (Lk., 1 Cor. iv 3, vi 2, James): ὁ ἐλαχιστότερος, the smallest, the least important: εἰς ἐλάχιστόν ἐστιν, it matters very little: ἐλάχιστον, adv. a very little.

ἐλαία.text: ἐλαία (olea), an olive tree: see ἐλαίων.
ἐλαία.note: Cross-reference is printed with the accent on the iota (ἐλαίων), although the headword it points to is printed Ἐλαιών; transcribed as printed.

ἔλαιον.text: ἔλαιον (oleum), olive-oil: ἔλαιον ἀγαλλιάσεως, oil of enjoyment, the oil with which the heads of guests at banquets are anointed, Heb. i 9.

ἐκφέρω.text: ἐκφέρω, I bring out, carry out, sometimes (effero) out of the city for burial; I bring forth, bear, Heb. vi 8.

ἐλεάω.note: Linked to the ἐλεέω entry, which gives ἐλεάω as a variant; the page also has a separate cross-reference entry: ἐλεάω, see ἐλεέω.

ἐλεύθερος.text: ἐλεύθερος, free (opposite of enslaved, cf. 1 Cor. xii 13).

ἐλέγχω.text: ἐλέγχω, (a) I reprove, rebuke: (b) I expose, show to be guilty, John iii 20, 1 Cor. xiv 24, Eph. v 11, 13, James ii 9.

ἐλεημοσύνη.text: ἐλεημοσύνη, abstr. alms-giving, charity: concr. alms, charity.

ἐλευθερία.text: ἐλευθερία, freedom, liberty, especially a state of freedom from slavery.

ἐλπίζω.text: ἐλπίζω (ἑλπίζω), I hope, hope for: the substantive following ἐν, εἰς, ἐπί with dat. or acc., is the ground of the hope, that which makes hope possible.

ἔμπροσθεν.text: ἔμπροσθεν, in front, before the face: sometimes made a substantive by the addition of the article; usually c. gen. in front of, before the face of.

ἐμφανίζω.text: ἐμφανίζω, I make visible (manifest); hence, act. I report (inform) against, Ac. xxiv 1, xxv 2, 15; pass. (quasi-technical) I appear before.
ἐμφανίζω.note: "quasi-technical" is broken across a line at the hyphen; kept as a real hyphen.

ἐμπίπτω.text: ἐμπίπτω, I fall in, am cast in.

ἐν.text: ἐν, (a) of place, in; ἐν τοῖς, see ὁ: ἐν Χριστῷ, of mystic indwelling; (b) = εἰς, into, e.g. Mt. x 16; (c) of time, in, during, at; (d) of instrument, (armed) with, Lk. xxii 49, 1 Cor. iv 21, &c.; (e) amounting to, Ac. vii 14 (cf. Mk. iv 8 bis); (f) consisting in, Eph. ii 15; (g) in the department of, cf. 1 Cor. vi 2; (h) in the judgement of, cf. 1 Cor. xiv 11; (i) Hebraistic use, Mt. x 32, Lk. xii 8. For ἐν ᾧ, see ὅς.

ἐνδείκνυμι.text: ἐνδείκνυμι (in the middle voice ἐνδείκνυμαι only), I show forth.

ἐνδύω.text: ἐνδύω, I put on, clothe (another): mid. I clothe (myself), dress: hence, metaphorically, of acquiring qualities; = ἐπενδύομαι, 2 Cor. v 3.

ἐνεργέω.text: ἐνεργέω, (a) intr. I am at work, work; (b) tr. I work, the acc. expressing ‘that which is worked’, effect. In N.T. the word is generally connected with miraculous interpositions; (c) in the passive always with non-personal subject, as ἐνεργεῖν always with personal, I am made operative (effective), I am made to produce my appropriate result, I am set in operation, I am made to work. Mid. absent from N.T.

ἐνδυναμόω.text: ἐνδυναμόω, I fill with δύναμις (power) (almost = δυναμόω).

ἕνεκα.text: ἕνεκα, ἕνεκεν, εἵνεκεν, for the sake of, on account of: οὗ (neut.) εἵνεκεν, on account of which, wherefore, Lk. iv 18; τίνος ἕνεκα, on account of what, wherefore, why, Ac. xix 32.

ἐνίστημι.text: ἐνίστημι: only in the intr. tenses, I impend, am at hand, am present: perf. pcpl. ἐνεστηκώς (ἐνεστώς) as adj. present.

ἐγκόπτω.text: ἐνκόπτω, (I introduce an obstacle sharply in the way of a moving object, cf. Eng. colloquial ‘I strike in’) I block, check, hinder.
ἐγκόπτω.note: Souter spells the headword ἐνκόπτω (unassimilated); same word as the lemma ἐγκόπτω.

ἐντέλλομαι.text: ἐντέλλομαι, I give orders (injunctions, instructions, commands).

ἔνοχος.text: ἔνοχος (obnoxius), involved in, hence liable, generally with dat. (or gen.) of the punishment.

ἐνοικέω.text: ἐνοικέω, I dwell in, am settled (stationary) in.

ἔντιμος.text: ἔντιμος, (held precious, hence) precious; honoured, honourable in rank, &c., Lk. xiv 8.

ἐνώπιον.text: ἐνώπιον (vernacular, attested from saec. ii B.C.), before the face of, in the presence of; in the eyes of.

ἐξάγω.text: ἐξάγω, I lead out, sometimes to death, execution (duco).

ἔξεστι(ν).text: ἔξεστιν, impers. it is permitted (allowed), sometimes followed by acc. et inf.: ἐξόν ἐστιν = ἔξεστιν, the ἔστιν being understood in Ac. ii 29, 2 Cor. xii 4.

ἐξίστημι.text: ἐξίστημι, ἐξιστάω, ἐξιστάνω (lit. I remove from a standing position), (a) in tr. tenses (including ἐξέστᾰκα), I astonish, amaze; (b) in intr. tenses, I am astonished, amazed; I am out of my mind, I am mad, Mk. iii 21, 2 Cor. v 13.
ἐξίστημι.note: ἐξέστᾰκα is printed with a breve (short mark) over the second alpha, not a circumflex.

ἐξαποστέλλω.text: ἐξαποστέλλω, I send away out, I send forth (a person qualified for a task).

ἐξουσία.text: ἐξουσία, (a) power, authority, weight, especially moral authority, influence; in 1 Cor. xi 10 the authority which the wearing of the veil gives the woman, making her sacrosanct; c. gen. indicates over any one; (b) in a quasi-personal sense, derived from later Judaism, of a spiritual power, 1 Pet. iii 22, and hence of an earthly power (e.g. Lk. xii 11 and often, in combination with ἀρχή).

ἔξω.text: ἔξω, (a) adv. without; in ὁ ἔξω, &c. the adv. is equivalent to an adjective, τὰς ἔξω πόλεις, foreign cities, Ac. xxvi 11, ὁ ἔξω ἄνθρωπος, the outer (physical) nature, 2 Cor. iv 16, especially οἱ ἔξω, the outsiders, the non-Christians; (b) prep. c. gen. outside.

ἔξωθεν.text: ἔξωθεν, (a) from outside, from without; (b) outside, equivalent to ἔξω, both as adv. and as prep. (Mk. vii 15, Rev. xi 2, xiv 20, &c.); τὸ ἔξωθεν, the outside, &c., οἱ ἔξωθεν = οἱ ἔξω.

ἐξουθενέω.text: ἐξουθενέω, I set at nought, ignore, despise.

ἐξομολογέω.text: ἐξομολογέω, (a) I consent fully, agree out and out, Lk. xxii 6; (b) I confess, admit, acknowledge (cf. the early Hellenistic sense of the middle, I acknowledge a debt); (c) in certain passages there is a difficulty as to the sense: in Mt. xi 25 (Lk. x 21) the Vulgate (with the Sahidic) renders by confiteor, but modern scholars prefer either I give thanks or I praise.

ἑορτή.text: ἑορτή, a festival, feast, periodically recurring: ποιεῖν ἑορτήν, Ac. xviii 21 = ἑορτάζειν.

ἐπαγγέλλομαι.text: ἐπαγγέλλομαι, (a) I promise; (b) I profess, 1 Tim. ii 10, vi 21.

ἐπερωτάω.text: ἐπερωτάω = ἐρωτάω simply, I ask, question.

ἐπεί.text: ἐπεί, (a) after, Lk. vii 1 (v. l.), Ac. xiii 46 (v.l.); (b) for, since; (c) otherwise, Rom. xi 6. 22, 1 Cor. v 10, &c.

ἐπάνω.text: ἐπάνω, (a) adv. on the top, above; (b) prep. on the top of, above, over, on: met. of rule, over, Lk. xix 17, &c.; above, more than, Mk. xiv 5, 1 Cor. xv 6.

ἐπέρχομαι.text: ἐπέρχομαι, I come upon, sometimes with hostility.

ἐπέχω.text: ἐπέχω, (a) tr. I hold forth; (b) intr. (νοῦν being understood) I mark, pay attention (heed), note, Ac. iii 5, 1 Tim. iv 16: I delay, Ac. xix 22.

ἐπί.text: ἐπί, (a) c. gen. locally, on, upon; and so met. of that on which anything rests, e.g. ἐπ’ ἀληθείας, in truth: of authority over, e.g. Mt. xxiv 45: concerning, Gal. iii 16: in presence of, e.g. Mt. xxviii 14: at, in, Mk. xii 26: in (at) the time (period) of, e.g. Mk. ii 26; (b) c. dat. on, upon: near, e.g. Mt. xxiv 33: on the basis (ground) of, e.g. Mt. iv 4: on account of, e.g. Lk. v 5, ἐφ’ ᾧ (= ἐπὶ τούτῳ, ὅ, τι), in view of the fact that: over (cf. under (a)), Lk. xii 44: against, Lk. xii 52: in addition to, e.g. 2 Cor. vii 13: in, at, ἐπὶ τούτῳ, meantime, John iv 27: for, with a view to, cf. Ac. v 35; (c) c. acc. locally, on, upon, generally after verbs indicating motion, but afterwards more widely used, both lit. and met., ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό, in the same place, together, in all, cf. Ac. i 15, ii 47: near, to, towards (after word expressing motion, and then more widely), both lit. and met.: against: in addition to (cf. under (b)), Phil. ii 27: of number or degree attained, as far as, e.g. ἐπὶ πλεῖον, ἐφ’ ὅσον: of charge, rule, or power over: concerning, e.g. Lk. xxiii 28: on account of, with a view to, Mk. xv 24, John xix 24: of time, for, during, e.g. Lk. iv 25: of time, about, e.g. Lk. x 35.

ἐπιβάλλω.text: ἐπιβάλλω, (a) I throw upon, cast over, 1 Cor. vii 35, Rev. xviii 19 (v.l.); (b) I place upon; (c) I lay, with τὴν χεῖρα (τὰς χεῖρας), either with innocent, or with hostile, intent (= inicere manum [manus]); (d) intr. I strike upon, Mk. iv 37; (e) intr. τὸ ἐπιβάλλον μέρος, the share that falls to (belongs to) one, Lk. xv 12; (f) intr. ἐπιβαλὼν ἔκλαιεν, he set to and wept, Mk. xiv 72.
ἐπιβάλλω.note: In τὴν χεῖρα there is a stray mark over the rho (between ρ and α); read as χεῖρα. The alpha of ἐπιβαλὼν is poorly printed but legible.

ἐπιβαίνω.text: ἐπιβαίνω, (a) I set foot on, I step on; (b) I mount (a horse), board (a vessel).

ἐπιγινώσκω.text: ἐπιγινώσκω, I come to know by directing my attention to (ἐπί) him or it, I perceive, discern, recognize: aor. I found out.

ἐπιθυμία.text: ἐπιθυμία, eager (passionate) desire, passion: see ἐπιθυμέω.

ἐπικαλέω.text: ἐπικαλέω, (a) I call (name) by a supplementary (additional, alternative) name; (b) mid. I call upon, appeal to, address.

ἐπίγνωσις.text: ἐπίγνωσις, knowledge of a particular point (directed towards a particular object); perception, discernment, recognition; intuition.

ἐπιθυμέω.text: ἐπιθυμέω, I desire, long; ἐπιθυμίᾳ ἐπιθυμεῖν, Hebraistic, to long eagerly, Lk. xxii 15.

ἐπιζητέω.text: ἐπιζητέω, I seek after, search for, make inquiries about.

ἐπιδίδωμι.text: ἐπιδίδωμι, (a) tr. I hand in; (b) intr. I give way (to the wind), Ac. xxvii 15.

ἐπιδείκνυμι.text: ἐπιδείκνυμι, I show, display, point out, indicate; I prove, demonstrate, Ac. xviii 28, Heb. vi 17.

ἐπιλαμβάνομαι.text: ἐπιλαμβάνομαι, I lay hold of, take hold of, seize (sometimes with beneficent, sometimes with hostile, intent).

ἐπιμένω.text: ἐπιμένω, (a) I remain, tarry; (b) c. dat. I remain in, persist in.

ἐπίκειμαι.text: ἐπίκειμαι, (a) c. dat. or c. ἐπί et dat. I am placed upon, am laid upon, lie upon, am imposed; I press upon, Lk. v 1; (b) absol. I press hard, Ac. xxvii 20; I am insistent, insist, Lk. xxiii 23.

ἐπιστρέφω.text: ἐπιστρέφω, (a) tr. I turn (back) to (towards); (b) intr. I turn (back) (to [towards]); I come to myself, Lk. xxii 32.

ἐπιπίπτω.text: ἐπιπίπτω, I fall upon; I press upon, Mk. iii 10.

ἐπισκέπτομαι.text: ἐπισκέπτομαι, (a) I look out, Ac. vi 3; (b) I visit.

ἐπιστάτης.text: ἐπιστάτης, master, teacher (cf. Dalman, Words of Jesus, Eng. tr., p. 276).

ἐπιτίθημι.text: ἐπιτίθημι, I place upon, lay on: with ὄνομα, I add, give in addition.

ἐπιτιμάω.text: ἐπιτιμάω, (a) I rebuke, chide, censure; (b) c. ἵνα, I warn.

ἐπιταγή.text: ἐπιταγή, instruction, command, order, authority (often of a god).

ἐπιφάνεια.text: ἐπιφάνεια, appearing, manifestation (of a conspicuous intervention from the sky on behalf of a worshipper).

ἔργον.text: ἔργον, (a) work, labour (in the physical, originally in the agricultural, sphere); (b) moral action, deed, hence with adjectives or genitives defining its character.

ἑπτά.text: ἑπτά, seven: οἱ ἑπτά, the seven (‘deacons’ of Ac. vi 3–6).

ἐργάζομαι.text: ἐργάζομαι, (a) I am at work, I work; (b) tr. I produce by work, put in force, give operation to, realize, e.g. Mt. vii 23; c. cogn. acc. ἔργον, ἔργα, Mt. xxvi 10, &c.; c. acc. βρῶσιν, I work for, John vi 27.

ἐπουράνιος.text: ἐπουράνιος (opp. ἐπίγειος), heavenly, in heaven: ἐν τοῖς ἐπουρανίοις, in the heavenly sphere, the sphere of spiritual activities.

ἐργάτης.text: ἐργάτης, a field-labourer; then, a labourer, workman in general.

ἐποικοδομέω.text: ἐποικοδομέω, I build upon (above) a foundation.

ἐργασία.text: ἐργασία, working, activity, work, service, trade, business, gains of business: δὸς ἐργασίαν (da operam), take pains to, see to it that you, Lk. xii 58; performance, practice, Eph. iv 19.

ἔρχομαι.text: ἔρχομαι, (a) I go: with acc. of extent, ὁδόν; (b) I come: εἰς ἑαυτὸν ἐλθών, having come to himself, having come to his right mind, ‘having reasoned with himself’ (Sahidic), Lk. xv 17.

ἐρωτάω.text: ἐρωτάω, (a) I ask (a question), I question; (b) (= αἰτέω) I request, make a request to; I pray.
ἐρωτάω.note: The mark after "make a request to" appears to be a semicolon, as transcribed.

ἔρημος.text: ἔρημος (the Latin heremus may be due to false analogy with heres, hereticus, &c.), adj. desert; hence, ἡ ἔρημος (sc. χώρα), the desert, to the E. and S. of Palestine: of a person, deserted, abandoned, desolate, Gal. iv 27.

ἐσθίω.text: ἐσθίω, ἔσθω, tr. and intr. I eat, I am eating; I take a meal: aor. φαγεῖν, to eat, but in Rev. x 10 = καταφαγεῖν.

ἕτερος.text: ἕτερος (alter), (a) of two, another, a second: ἐν ἑτέρῳ (sc. ψαλμῷ), Heb. v 6; ὁ ἕτερος, the other, the second, τῇ ἑτέρᾳ (sc. ἡμέρᾳ), on the second day, Ac. xx 15, xxvii 3; ἕτεροι, others, another group; (b) sometimes it does not differ from ἄλλος (alius), being used of more than two, other, different, cf. Lk. viii 6–8, 2 Cor. xi 4: in Gal. i 6 f. ἕτερος appears to mean another of the same kind, as contrasted with ἄλλος, another of a different kind.

ἔσχατος.text: ἔσχατος (ultimus), last: ἔσχατον, neut. acc. as adv., at the last, finally; ἐπ’ ἐσχάτου, at the end; ἕως ἐσχάτου, till the end.

ἔσωθεν.text: ἔσωθεν, (a) from within, from inside; (b) within, inside: τὸ ἔσωθεν, the inner part, the inner element.

ἔτι.text: ἔτι (adhuc), (a) of time, still, yet; even now: οὐκ ἔτι, no longer, and similarly with other negatives; (b) of degree, even; further, more, in addition.

εὐαγγέλιον.text: εὐαγγέλιον, τό, the good news of the coming of the Messiah, the gospel: the gen. after it expresses sometimes the giver (God), sometimes the subject (the Messiah, &c.), sometimes the human transmitter (an apostle).

εὐαγγελίζω.text: εὐαγγελίζω, but far oftener mid. εὐαγγελίζομαι, I bring good news, I preach good tidings, with or without an obj., expressing either the persons who receive the good news or the good news itself (the good news being sometimes expressed as a person, e.g. Ac. v 42).

ἔτος.text: ἔτος, ἕτος, a year: κατ’ ἔτος (καθ’ ἕτος), annually; ἀπὸ or ἐξ ἐτῶν followed by a number (Fr. depuis, Germ. seit, English for), lit. from . . . years.
ἔτος.note: The breathings on the second headword and on the word after καθ’ are hard to read at this resolution; their shape (and καθ’) indicate rough breathing, so read as ἕτος.

ἕτοιμος.text: ἕτοιμος, ready, prepared: ἐν ἑτοίμῳ ἔχοντες, being ready, 2 Cor. x 6, cf. ἑτοίμως.

εὐθύς.text: εὐθύς, adv. immediately: characteristic of Mk.
εὐθύς.note: link corrected and transcribed from the page image by Claude, 2026-11-09

εὐδοκέω.text: εὐδοκέω, I am well-pleased, c. acc. expressing with, Mt. xii 18, &c.; I think it good, am resolved (a characteristic word of Jewish Greek).

εὐδοκία.text: εὐδοκία, (a) good-will (good-pleasure), favour, feeling of complacency of God to man: ἄνθρωποι εὐδοκίας (Hebraistic), men with whom God is well-pleased, Lk. ii 14; (b) good-pleasure, satisfaction, happiness, delight of men, e. g. 2 Thess. i 11, though even in such passages there may be a latent reference to (divine) approval.

εὐλογέω.text: εὐλογέω, (lit. I speak well of, opp. I abuse, curse) I bless; εὐλογημένος, of a man, blessed (by God; contrast εὐλογητός): εὐλογῶν (or ἐν εὐλογίᾳ) εὐλογῶ (Hebraistic), I bless abundantly.

εὐλογητός.text: εὐλογητός (used only of God), blessed (as entitled to receive blessing from man).

εὑρίσκω.text: εὑρίσκω (reperio), I find, especially after searching; but in Phil. iii 9 possibly I surprise.

εὐχαριστέω.text: εὐχαριστέω, I give thanks: pass. 3 sing. is received with thanks, 2 Cor. i 11.

εὐφραίνω.text: εὐφραίνω, I cheer, make glad: generally mid. or pass. I am glad; I make merry, revel, feast.

εὐσχήμων.text: εὐσχήμων, (a) comely, seemly, decorous; (b) of honourable position (in society).

ἔχω.text: ἔχω, (a) tr. I hold, have, possess; ἔσχον, generally, I got, received, acquired, ἔσχηκα, I possessed; ἔχω τι κατά (εἰς), I have a ground of complaint against; ἐν γαστρὶ ἔχειν, to have (a child) in the womb; with double acc., the second being in the pred. (with or without εἰς), to have so and so as . . ., to regard so and so as (cf. Mk. xi 32); with obj. indicating time (cf. Fr. avoir) to be so and so days &c. old; (b) c. infin. I am able; (c) c. adv. equal to εἰμί with corresponding adjective; (d) intr. κατὰ κεφαλῆς ἔχων, having a covering over the head, with head covered, 1 Cor. xi 4; (e) Mid. I am neighbouring, I am next to, e. g. Mk. i 38, τῇ ἐχομένῃ (sc. ἡμέρᾳ), next day, Lk. xiii 33, cf. Ac. xiii 44 (v.l.), &c.
ἔχω.note: The letter in '(e) Mid.' is faint on the image and could be read as (c); (e) follows the sequence (a)-(d). The breathing and accent on εἰς (twice) are small and hard to make out.

ἐφίστημι.text: ἐφίστημι: in intr. tenses and passive, I come upon (suddenly or unexpectedly) and stand by: met. I press forward, 2 Tim. iv 2.

ἕως.text: ἕως, (a) conj. until: followed by the indic. where a definite time in the past is indicated; with or without οὗ or ὅτου, and followed by the subjunctive aorist with, or without, ἂν or ἐάν, indicating an indefinite time, until . . . shall have, e. g. ἕως ἂν πάντα γένηται, until all shall have happened, Mt. v 18; (b) prep. as far as, up to, as much as, until, both in local and temporal connexions, both with nouns in gen. and with adverbs (or prepositions).

ζάω.text: ζάω, I live; ἑαυτῷ ζῆν, to be one’s own master.

ζῆλος.text: ζῆλος (masc. and neut.), (a) eagerness, zeal, enthusiasm; (b) jealousy, rivalry.

ζωή.text: ζωή, life, both of physical (present) and of spiritual (particularly future) existence; sometimes, e. g. Mk. x 17, = Hebrew ḥayyīm (a plural form) = all the days you are alive (nearer to βίος than ζωή), of a place in the New Age.

ζύμη.text: ζύμη, leaven, ferment, both lit. and met.

ζηλόω.text: ζηλόω, (a) intr. I am jealous; (b) tr. I am jealous of, with acc. of a person; I am eager for, I am eager to possess, with acc. of a thing.

ζήτησις.note: Headword print is damaged (the iota is broken), and the mark after it looks like a semicolon, probably a blemish for Souter's usual comma; transcribed as a comma.

ζήτημα.text: ζήτημα (quaestio), a question, subject of inquiry.

ἤ.text: ἤ, (a) or, both in rel. and interrog. clauses: in interrog. sentences we ought perhaps sometimes to accent ἦ (cf. εἰ) and regard simply as an interrogative particle, not to be translated; (b) than, sometimes almost otiose after πρίν; ἀλλ’ ἤ (Lk. xii 51, 2 Cor. i 13) should be ἄλλ’ ἤ (i. e. ἄλλο ἤ), nothing but; ἢ γάρ in Lk. xviii 14 (v.l.) is corrupt.
ἤ.note: Breathings and accents on the small Greek forms are faint: headword read as ἤ, 'accent ἦ' (circumflex), '(cf. εἰ)' (breathing only), and 'ἢ γάρ' (grave).

ἤδη.text: ἤδη, already; now at length, now after all this waiting Rom. i 10.

ἡγέομαι.text: ἡγέομαι, (a) I lead: ὁ ἡγούμενος (as subst.), the leader; (b) (cf. duco) I think, I am of opinion.

ἥκω.text: ἥκω, I have come, but other tenses are translated as if the present meant I come.

ἡγεμών.text: ἡγεμών (praeses, a very wide word), a (Roman) governor.

ζῳοποιέω.text: ζωοποιέω, I make that which was dead to live.

ἡμέρα.text: ἡμέρα (dies), a day, the period from sunrise to sunset; (ἡ) ἡμέρα κρίσεως, ἡ ἡμέρα ἐκείνη, ἡ ἡμέρα τοῦ κυρίου, the judgement day, coinciding with the end of the world, according to late Jewish belief; τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ, &c., on the third day, after two days, so διὰ τριῶν ἡμερῶν, Mt. xxvi 61, &c.; νύκτα καὶ ἡμέραν, through night as well as day; νυκτὸς καὶ ἡμέρας, by night as well as day, imply merely before dawn as well as during the day; (τὸ) καθ’ ἡμέραν, day by day, each day; πάσας τὰς ἡμέρας (vernacular phrase), perpetually, Mt. xxviii 20.
ἡμέρα.note: In 'πάσας τὰς ἡμέρας' the print of πάσας is blurred (could be misread as πάσης); also the final '20' is faint.

ἥλιος.text: ἥλιος, the sun; μὴ βλέπων τὸν ἥλιον, equivalent to stone-blind, Ac. xiii 11.

θάνατος.text: θάνατος, death, physical or spiritual; θάνατοι appears to mean risks to life, 2 Cor. xi 23; ὁ δεύτερος θάνατος (ὁ θάνατος ὁ δεύτερος), the death of the spiritual part in man, practically annihilation of personality.

θάλασσα.text: θάλασσα, (a) the sea, in contrast to the land (γῆ): τὸ πέλαγος τῆς θαλάσσης (tautol.), the depth of the sea, Mt. xviii 6; (b) a particular sea or lake, e. g. the sea of Galilee (Tiberias), the Red Sea.

θέλω.text: θέλω, (a) intr. I will; οὐ θέλω, I refuse; θέλειν ἐν, to fix one’s will on, to stick resolutely to, Col. ii 18; followed by subj. with, or without, ἵνα, I will that; (b) tr. I wish, desire.

θέλημα.text: θέλημα, an act of will, will; plur. wishes, desires; τὸ θέλημα τοῦ θεοῦ, the will of God, sometimes as a will to be recognized, sometimes as a will to be obeyed.

θαυμάζω.text: θαυμάζω, (a) intr. I wonder; cognate acc. θαυμάζειν θαῦμα μέγα, Rev. xvii 6, to wonder very greatly; (b) tr. I wonder at, admire.

θεμέλιος.text: θεμέλιος (properly an adj. belonging to the foundation, with λίθος understood), a foundation stone; plur. neut. θεμέλια is used, Ac. xvi 26.

θεός.text: θεός, (a) a god or goddess, John x 34, 35, Ac. vii 40, xiv 11, xix 26, 37, 1 Cor. viii 5, Gal. iv 8; (b) the god. The word is an appellative. The Christian, like the Jew and many pagans, avoided naming his God, and referred to him as the god.

θεραπεύω.text: θεραπεύω, I care for, attend, serve, treat, especially of a physician; hence I heal, sometimes with ἀπό, of.

θεμελιόω.text: θεμελιόω, I found, lit. and met.

θηρίον.text: θηρίον, properly a wild beast, hence any animal.

θησαυρός.text: θησαυρός, a store-house for precious things; hence a treasure, a store.

θλίβω.text: θλίβω, (a) I make narrow (strictly by pressure), Mt. vii 14; I press upon, Mk. iii 9; (b) I persecute, press hard.

θνῄσκω.text: θνῄσκω, I am dying: perf. τέθνηκα, I am dead; τεθνηκώς, dead.

θησαυρίζω.text: θησαυρίζω, I store up, I treasure up, I save.

θύρα.text: θύρα, (a) a door; (b) met. an opportunity, Ac. xiv 27, 1 Cor. xvi 9, &c.

θυγάτηρ.text: θυγάτηρ, a daughter; hence (Hebraistic?), of any female descendant, however far removed, Lk. i 5, xiii 16; even of one unrelated, my young lady, Mk. v 34, &c.

θυσία.text: θυσία, abstr. and concr., sacrifice; a sacrifice.

θυμός.text: θυμός, an outburst of passion, wrath.

θύω.text: θύω, I sacrifice, generally an animal; hence I kill.

ἴδιος.text: ἴδιος (ἴδιος) (proprius), one’s own, belonging to one, private, personal: οἱ ἴδιοι, one’s own people, one’s own family, John i 11; ὁ ἴδιος, possibly his own (son), Ac. xx 28; τὰ ἴδια, one’s own home, one’s own property, John i 11, &c.; ἰδίᾳ, κατ’ ἰδίαν (καθ’ ἰδίαν) (possibly sc. ὁδόν), privately, apart, in private, by oneself, individually.
ἴδιος.note: Breathing on the parenthetical variant is small: read as rough (ἵδιος), smooth on the headword. | David 2026-11-09: ἴδιος (ἵδιος) → ἴδιος (ἴδιος)

ἰάομαι.text: ἰάομαι, I heal, generally of physical, sometimes of spiritual, disease.

ἱερεύς.text: ἱερεύς, a priest, one who offers sacrifice to a god (in Jewish and pagan religions; of Christians only metaphorically).

ἱκανός.text: ἱκανός, (a) considerable, sufficient, of number, quantity, time: ἐξ ἱκανῶν χρόνων (v. l. ἱκανοῦ), already for a long time, Lk. xxiii 8 (cf. viii 27), ἐφ’ ἱκανόν, for a sufficiently long time, Ac. xx 11; ἱκανόν ἐστιν, enough of this subject, Lk. xxii 38 (cf. 2 Cor. ii 6); τὸ ἱκανὸν ποιεῖν τινι (satis facere alicui), to satisfy one, to give him no ground of complaint, Mk. xv 15, τὸ ἱκανὸν λαμβάνω (satis accipio), I get surety (security), Ac. xvii 9; (b) of persons, sufficiently strong (good, &c.), worthy, suitable, with various constructions.

ἵνα.text: ἵνα, (A) in statements: (a) indicating purpose, in order that; (b) indicating a command or wish, Mk. v 23, vi 25, x 35, 51, John xvii 24, 1 Cor. vii 29, 2 Cor. viii 7, Gal. ii 10, Eph. v 33; (c) indicating consequence, so that, e. g. Rom. xi 11; (d) a mere introduction to a noun clause, that, e. g. John xvii 3; (B) in interrogations: ἵνα τί (ut quid), why? wherefore?

ἱμάτιον.text: ἱμάτιον, a long flowing outer garment.

ἵστημι.text: ἱστάνω (form appearing first in 3rd cent. B.C.), ἵστημι, (a) tr. in tenses of the active mood (including new perf. -έστακα), except 2 aor. and perf. (form ἕστηκα) and plup., I make to stand, I set up: I weigh (pay), Mt. xxvi 15; (b) intr. in 2 aor. and perf. (form ἕστηκα) and plup., also mid. and pass., I am set up, I am made to stand, I stand, I take an erect position, I stand firm: = ἀντιστῆναι, Eph. vi 13.
ἵστημι.note: Souter's combined entry for ἱστάνω and ἵστημι.

ἰσχυρός.text: ἰσχυρός, strong (originally and generally of physical strength); powerful.

ἰσχύω.text: ἰσχύω, I have strength, I am strong, I am in full health and vigour (opp. κακῶς ἔχω) Mt. ix 12; and so I am able, sometimes followed by the inf. or εἰς c. acc. to indicate the purpose for which the strength is used, e. g. Mt. xxvi 40, v 13; c. acc. adverbially, qualifying the strength, τι ἰσχύει, has any validity (value), Gal. v 6, cf. Heb. ix 17, πάντα ἰσχύω, I have all strength (power), Phil. iv 13, πολὺ ἰσχύει, has great power, James v 16.

καθαρίζω.text: καθαρίζω (alternative spelling καθερίζω, perhaps = καθαιρίζω, but it occurs only in augmented and reduplicated forms and has been otherwise explained) (purgo), I make clean, literally, ceremonially, or spiritually, according to context, ἀπό c. gen. being sometimes added, of the dirt removed.

καθαρός.text: καθαρός (purus), clean, pure, unstained, either literally or ceremonially or spiritually; καθαρὸς ἀπό, unstained by.

καθάπερ.text: καθάπερ (i. e. καθ’ ἅπερ, according to which things), even as.
καθάπερ.note: The apostrophe after καθ is faint or missing on the image (cf. the καθά entry just above, which prints καθ’ ἅ); transcribed as καθ’.

καθαρισμός.text: καθαρισμός, cleansing, purifying, purification, literal, ceremonial, or moral.

καί.text: καί, and; sometimes modifying a following word, even.

καθώς.text: καθώς, according to the manner in which, in the degree that, as.

κάθημαι.text: κάθημαι, I am seated, I sit: καθήμενος, seated, sitting.

καθίζω.text: καθίζω, (a) tr. I make to sit, I set; (b) intr. aor. I sat down.

καθεύδω.text: καθεύδω, I am sleeping (asleep), I sleep.

καθίστημι.text: καθίστημι, καθιστάνω, in the tr. tenses (see ἵστημι), I set, establish, appoint, constitute, make; I conduct, Ac. xvii 15: καθίσταται, shows itself, acts its part, James iii 6.

καιρός.text: καιρός, fitting season, season, opportunity, occasion, time: πρὸς καιρόν, for a time.

κακός.text: κακός, bad, evil, in the widest sense.

καίω.text: καίω, tr. I ignite, I light, I burn, lit. and met.

κακία.text: κακία, (a) evil (i. e. trouble, labour, misfortune), Mt. vi 34; (b) wickedness, Ac. viii 22; (c) vicious disposition, malice, spite.

καρδία.text: καρδία (Lat. cor, Hebr. lēb, lēbab), (A) lit. the heart, as an organ of the body; (B) mind covers the non-physical sense best: (a) personality, character, inner life (illa uis qua cogitationes fiunt, Augustine, De nat. et orig. animae iv 6 § 7), e. g. 1 Cor. xiv 25, 1 Pet. i 22; (b) emotional state, e. g. Rom. ix 2; (c) mind, intellect, e. g. Rom. i 21; (d) will, volition, intention, e. g. Rom. ii 5.
καρδία.note: Targets list this under page 130, but the entry is printed on page 131 (page 130 ends at καπηλεύω).

καλέω.text: καλέω, (a) I call, summon, invite; (b) I call, name: ἐπί, after, Lk. i 59.

καλός.text: καλός (honestus), beautiful, as an outward sign of the inward good, noble, honourable character; good, worthy, honourable, noble, and seen to be so.

καλῶς.text: καλῶς, well, nobly, honourably; in a good place, James ii 3: compar. κάλλιον; καλῶς ποιήσεις, especially with aor. participle, is idiomatic for please, 3 John 6, cf. Ac. x 33, Phil. iv 14, 2 Pet. i 19.

κακῶς.text: κακῶς, badly, evilly: κακῶς ἔχω, see ἔχω.

καπνός.note: Targets list this under page 130, but the entry is printed at the top of page 131.

κάλαμος.text: κάλαμος, a reed; a reed-pen, 3 John 13.

κατά.text: κατά, (A) c. gen.: (a) against, Mt. xii 30; (b) down from, Mt. viii 32, κατὰ κεφαλῆς, down over the head, on the head, 1 Cor. xi 4; (c) throughout, Lk. iv 14, xxiii 5, Ac. ix 31, x 37, always with ὅλος; ἡ κατὰ βάθους πτωχεία, deep (abject) poverty, 2 Cor. viii 2; (d) in oaths, by, Mt. xxvi 63, Heb. vi 13, 16; (B) c. acc. (lit. down along): (a) over against, Ac. ii 10, xvi 7; (b) among, νόμος ὁ καθ’ ὑμᾶς, the law among you, your law, Ac. xviii 15, cf. xvii 28, xxvi 3, Eph. i 15, Col. iv 7, &c.; (c) with distributive force, (τὸ) καθ’ ἡμέραν, daily, day by day, each day, κατὰ ἑορτήν, at each feast, Mt. xxvii 15, Mk. xv 6, κατὰ ἑκατόν, by hundreds, Mk. vi 40, ungrammatically εἷς κατὰ (καθ’) εἷς, Mk. xiv 19, [John] viii 9 (contrast Eph. v 33), τὸ δὲ καθ’ εἷς (καθεῖς), singly, with reference to each individual, Rom. xii 5, &c.; (d) according to, by way of, Mt. ii 16, καθ’ ὅσον, &c.; in titles of Gospels, κατά practically indicates the author; (e) various adverbial phrases: τὸ κατ’ ἐμέ, as far as in me lies, with πρόθυμος, Rom. i 15, cf. τὸ κατὰ σάρκα, Rom. ix 5, &c.; κατ’ (καθ’) ἰδίαν (ἱδίαν) (opp. δημοσίᾳ), privately, by oneself, individually, Mt. xiv 13, &c.; κατὰ μόνας, alone, Mk. iv 10, Lk. ix 18; κατὰ πρόσωπον, in a Hebraistic periphrasis, in the presence of, Lk. ii 31, Ac. iii 13, cf. xxv 16.
κατά.note: Breathings on ἰδίαν (ἱδίαν) (continuation on p. 132) too small to read on the image; given as smooth then rough, matching κατ’ (καθ’).

καρπός.text: καρπός (fructus), (a) fruit, generally vegetable, sometimes animal (e.g. Lk. i 42, Ac. ii 30); (b) met. fruit, deed, action, result, Mt. iii 8, Lk. iii 8, James iii 17 f., &c.; (c) profit, gain, Rom. i 13, &c.

καρποφορέω.text: καρποφορέω (fructifico), act. and mid. I bear fruit.

καταβαίνω.text: καταβαίνω, I go down, I come down, either from the sky or from higher land.

καταβολή.text: καταβολή, (a) foundation, only in Mt. xiii 35 without κόσμου (add. v. l.); (b) depositing, sowing, deposit, σπέρματος, technically used of the act of conception, Heb. xi 11.

καταισχύνω.text: καταισχύνω, I shame, disgrace, bring to shame, put to utter confusion.

καταλαμβάνω.text: καταλαμβάνω, (A) act. (a) I seize tight hold of, arrest, catch, capture, appropriate, Mk. ix 18, [John] viii 3, 4, Rom. ix 30, 1 Cor. ix 24, Phil. iii 12, 13; (b) I overtake, John i 5, vi 17 (v.l.), xii 35, 1 Thess. v 4; (B) mid. aor. I perceived, comprehended.

κατάκειμαι.text: κατάκειμαι, I recline (at table); more often, I keep my bed, I am lying ill (in bed).

καταλείπω.text: καταλείπω, I leave behind; I desert, abandon.

καταλύω.text: καταλύω (lit. I loosen thoroughly), (a) tr. I break up, overthrow, destroy, both lit. and met., ὁ καταλύων, you would-be destroyer (of), Mt. xxvii 40; (b) I unyoke, unharness a carriage horse or pack animal; hence I put up, I lodge, I find a lodging, Lk. ix 12, xix 7.

κατανοέω.text: κατανοέω, I understand, take in a fact about, take knowledge of, take notice of, perceive; I detect, Lk. xx 23; I master, Ac. vii 31.

καταντάω.text: καταντάω, (a) I come down, either from high land to lower (or actually to the sea-coast), or from the high seas to the coast; hence met. I reach (my destination), Ac. xxvi 7, Eph. iv 13, Phil. iii 11; (b) of property, I come down (descend) by inheritance to an heir, 1 Cor. x 11, xiv 36.

καταργέω.text: καταργέω, (a) I make idle (inactive), I make of no effect, I annul, abolish, bring to naught; (b) with ἀπό, I discharge, sever, separate from.

καταρτίζω.text: καταρτίζω, (a) I fit (join) together, Mk. i 19, Mt iv 21; met. I compact together, 1 Cor. i 10; (b) act. and mid. I prepare, I perfect, for his (its) full destination or use, I bring into its proper condition (whether for the first time, or after a lapse).
καταρτίζω.note: "Mt iv 21" is printed without a period after Mt; kept as printed.

κατασκευάζω.text: κατασκευάζω, I build, construct, prepare, make.

καταπίνω.text: καταπίνω, (a) (originally of liquids, extended to solids) I drink up, swallow, gulp down; I gobble; (b) pass. lit. and met. I drown, am drowning.

καταπέτασμα.text: καταπέτασμα (lit. that which is spread out downwards, that which hangs down), curtain, of that which separated the Holy of Holies from the outer parts of the temple at Jerusalem, also of an outer curtain at the entrance to the Holy Place in the same temple; the latter is strictly denoted by κάλυμμα; yet Heb. ix 3 speaks of the former as τὸ δεύτερον καταπέτασμα.

καταφρονέω.text: καταφρονέω, I despise, scorn, and show it by active insult.

κατοικέω.text: κατοικέω, I dwell in (implying a more permanent settlement than παροικέω), I settle in, I am established in (permanently).

κατεργάζομαι.text: κατεργάζομαι, I work out; I produce, accomplish.

κατηγορέω.text: κατηγορέω (accuso), I accuse, charge; I prosecute.

κατέχω.text: κατέχω, (a) I hold fast, bind, arrest; (b) I take possession of, lay hold of, Lk. xiv 9; (c) I hold back, detain, restrain, Lk. iv 42, Rom. i 18, 2 Thess. ii 6, 7, Philem. 13; (d) I hold a ship (sc. τὴν ναῦν), keep its head, Ac. xxvii 40.

κατέρχομαι.text: κατέρχομαι, I come down from sky to earth, or from high land to lower land (or to the coast), or from the high seas to the shore: pcpl. qualitative in James iii 15.

καυχάομαι.text: καυχάομαι, I boast; I glory (exult) proudly.

κεῖμαι.text: κεῖμαι, a perf. used instead of the perf. pass. of τίθημι, I have been placed (put, laid), hence, I lie: the former sense explains the construction with εἰς and acc.

καύχημα.text: καύχημα, a boasting, a ground of boasting (glorying, exultation).

κάτω.text: κάτω, (a) down, below, also downwards; (b) compar. κατωτέρω, lower, under, less, of a length of a time, Mt. ii 16.

κενός.text: κενός, (a) empty; (b) met. empty (in moral content), vain, ineffective, foolish, worthless; εἰς κενόν, in vain, to no purpose; (c) false, unreal, pretentious, hollow, Eph. v 6, Col. ii 8, James ii 20.

κερδαίνω.text: κερδαίνω, I gain: ὕβριν καὶ ζημίαν, I gain injury and loss, i.e. I gain by shunning injury and loss, I do not suffer (I am spared) injury and loss, Ac. xxvii 21.

κέρας.text: κέρας, (a) a horn; (b) as a symbol of strength, κέρας σωτηρίας, a powerful support of salvation, Lk. i 69; (c) a dwarfed column set upon or at the corner of an altar, with ritual significance, Rev. ix 13.

κεφαλή.text: κεφαλή, (a) head, κατὰ κεφαλῆς ἔχων, see κατά; (b) met. κεφαλὴ γωνίας, a corner stone, uniting two walls, Mk. xii 10 and parallels; head, ruler, lord, 1 Cor. xi 3, &c.

κλάδος.text: κλάδος, a branch of a tree.

κλαίω.text: κλαίω, I weep; c. acc. or ἐπί c. acc. I weep for, mourn.

κληρονομέω.text: κληρονομέω, I inherit, I obtain (possess) by inheritance.

κληρονόμος.text: κληρονόμος, an heir, an inheritor: cf. κληρονομία.

κληρονομία.text: κληρονομία, an inheritance, an heritage, regularly the gift of God to His chosen people, in O. T. the Promised Land, in N. T. a possession viewed in one sense as present, in another as future.

κλέπτω.text: κλέπτω, I steal; ὁ κλέπτων, the stealer, Eph. iv 28.

κλῆρος.text: κλῆρος, (a) a lot; (b) a portion assigned, Ac. i 17, viii 21, xxvi 18, Col. i 12; hence, a portion of the people of God assigned to one’s care, a congregation, 1 Pet. v 3.

κοιλία.text: κοιλία, belly, abdomen, a general term covering any organ in the abdomen, e.g. stomach, womb: ἐκ κοιλίας μητρός, from birth.

κοιμάομαι.text: κοιμάομαι, I fall asleep, I am asleep, sometimes of the sleep of death (e.g. Mt. xxvii 52).

κλῆσις.text: κλῆσις, a calling, invitation, summons of God to the religious life; sometimes, e.g. Phil. iii 14, 2 Thess. i 11, Heb. iii 1, it may include a reference to the final issue of this invitation.

κλητός.text: κλητός, called, invited, summoned by God to the religious life.

κοινωνία.text: κοινωνία, (lit. partnership) (a) contributory help, Ac. ii 42, Rom. xv 26, 2 Cor. viii 4, ix 13, Heb. xiii 16; (b) sharing in, Phil. i 5, iii 10, Philem. 6, cf. (c); (c) spiritual fellowship, a fellowship in the spirit, 1 Cor. i 9, x 16, 2 Cor. vi 14, xiii 13, Gal. ii 9, Phil. ii 1, 1 John i 3, 6, 7 (frequently outside N.T., of the marriage relationship).

κοινός.text: κοινός, (a) common, shared; (b) Hebraistic use (in contrast to ἅγιος), profane; dirty, unclean, unwashed, Mk. vii 2, Ac. x 14, 28, xi 8, Rom. xiv 14, Heb. x 29, Rev. xxi 27.

κοινόω.text: κοινόω (cf. κοινός), (a) I make unclean, I pollute; (b) mid. I regard (treat) as unclean, Ac. x 15, xi 9.

κολλάομαι.text: κολλάω (lit. I glue): hence, mid. and pass. I join myself closely, I cleave, I adhere (to), I keep company (with), of friendly intercourse; of inanimate objects, Lk. x 11.
κολλάομαι.note: Headword printed as κολλάω (mid. and pass. sense covers κολλάομαι); entry continues onto p. 144.

κοινωνέω.text: κοινωνέω, (a) I share, communicate, contribute, impart, Rom. xii 13, Gal. vi 6; (b) I share in, I have a share of, I have fellowship with, c. gen. or dat.

κοπιάω.text: κοπιάω, (a) I grow weary, Mt. xi 28, John iv 6, Rev. ii 3; (b) I toil, work with effort (of bodily and mental labour alike).
